answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-work registry: before an agent may trade, it locks a deposit that grows with the volume it handles, so one operator spinning up a thousand puppets must fund every one. Reputation accrues only through completed, attested work, and a newcomer starts at the flat top of the mesa with zero trust. Like an opal, that history is hard to fake, its layered record shifting under inspection, while an onyx ledger entry, once written, cannot be rewritten. Sybils become expensive to create and worthless to run, because trust is earned in public, one exchange at a time.
